title: The New Supreme Court Cases to Watch

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin，我是 Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我那个黑胶唱片时代的夜店当 DJ 的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着 300 件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成了一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的 Sabrina Tavernisi，这是《The Daily》。

sentences.en: Last week, the Supreme Court began its new term, picking up where it left off on the most contentious issues of the day.
sentences.zh: 上周，最高法院开启了新一届任期，继续处理当前最具争议的议题。

sentences.en: But while previous terms produced major victories for the conservative legal movement, my colleague Adam Liptak explains today why this term may be different.
sentences.zh: 尽管此前的任期为保守派法律运动带来了重大胜利，但我的同事 Adam Liptak 今天将解释为什么这一届任期可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, October 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是 10 月 10 日，星期二。

sentences.en: Adam.
sentences.zh: Adam。

sentences.en: Hi, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 你好，Sabrina。

sentences.en: You're back, which means the Supreme Court is back.
sentences.zh: 你回来了，这意味着最高法院也回来了。

sentences.en: And we wanted to go to you, Adam, our trusted Supreme Court expert, to learn what big cases are coming up this term.
sentences.zh: 我们想找你，Adam，我们值得信赖的最高法院专家，来了解一下本届任期内即将审理的重大案件。

sentences.en: And, you know, we've had, of course, two terms of blockbuster cases that brought these huge changes to American society, you know, tugging it to the right.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们已经经历了两个充满重磅案件的任期，这些案件给美国社会带来了巨大变革，你知道的，把社会向右拉。

sentences.en: What do you expect to see this term?
sentences.zh: 你预计本届任期会看到什么？

sentences.en: I think this term will show us and bring into focus how far and how fast it wants to continue to move to the right.
sentences.zh: 我认为本届任期将向我们展示并聚焦它想要继续向右推进的程度和速度。

sentences.en: It has a lot of unfinished business from those earlier terMs.
sentences.zh: 它还有很多前几届任期留下的未竟事业。

sentences.en: It's facing a series of kind of follow-up cases in the areas of administrative law, agency power, the Second Amendment, gun rights, and abortion,
sentences.zh: 它正面临一系列后续案件，涉及行政法、机构权力、宪法第二修正案、持枪权和堕胎等领域，

sentences.en: all of which are cases in which conservative litigants and conservative courts are pushing hard in anticipation of a positive reception from the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所有这些案件中，保守派诉讼方和保守派法院都在积极推动，期待得到最高法院的积极回应。

sentences.en: So you're saying that conservative legal activists watch this 6-3 majority, make major rulings on these three issues.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，保守派法律活动人士在观察这 6 比 3 的多数派，并在这些议题上做出重大裁决。

sentences.en: And now they see an open door and they want to push it to see how much farther they can go.
sentences.zh: 现在他们看到了敞开的大门，想要推一把，看看还能走多远。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So, Adam, let's dig into this.
sentences.zh: 那么，Adam，让我们深入探讨一下。

sentences.en: So let's start with the administrative state, which, of course, I know is kind of a thing out there.
sentences.zh: 我们先从行政国家说起，我知道这在外面是个热门话题。

sentences.en: But what exactly is that?
sentences.zh: 但那到底是什么？

sentences.en: Start with the definition and then tell me about that case.
sentences.zh: 先给个定义，然后跟我讲讲那个案子。

sentences.en: So for the longest time, the conservative legal movement has really despised the idea that unelected bureaucrats,
sentences.zh: 长期以来，保守派法律运动一直非常鄙视那种非民选官僚的想法，

sentences.en: experts who work in agencies like the Environmental Protection Agency or the Food and Drug Administration,
sentences.zh: 也就是在环境保护署（EPA）或食品药品监督管理局（FDA）等机构工作的专家，

sentences.en: that they would say are unaccountable to the American public, get to make major decisions about American life that they say belongs to Congress, or if not to Congress,
sentences.zh: 他们认为这些人不对美国公众负责，却能对美国生活做出重大决定，而他们认为这些决定本应属于国会，如果不是国会，

sentences.en: to the courts, but not to what they would call, you know, these deep state experts.
sentences.zh: 也应属于法院，而不是他们所说的那些“深层政府”专家。

sentences.en: And in various ways, they've tried to withdraw power from the agencies, and this term comes on the heels of two blockbuster decisions in the last term and the one before,
sentences.zh: 他们以各种方式试图收回这些机构的权力，而本届任期紧随上届和上上届的两个重磅裁决之后，

sentences.en: one of them making it hard for the EPA to address climate change, the other striking down President Biden's student loan forgiveness program,
sentences.zh: 其中一个裁决让 EPA 难以应对气候变化，另一个则推翻了拜登总统的学生贷款减免计划，

sentences.en: both of them saying that the executive branch had gone too far and gone beyond what Congress had authorized.
sentences.zh: 两者都认为行政部门做得太过火了，超出了国会的授权范围。

sentences.en: And those cases set the stage for the new cases this term.
sentences.zh: 这些案件为本届任期的新案件奠定了基础。

sentences.en: So what about this term?
sentences.zh: 那么本届任期呢？

sentences.en: What about these new cases?
sentences.zh: 这些新案件是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Well, the biggest case asks the court to overrule really the foundational precedent in this area, a 40-year-old precedent called Chevron,
sentences.zh: 嗯，最大的案子要求法院推翻该领域真正的基础性先例，一个 40 年前的先例，叫做“雪佛龙案”（Chevron），

sentences.en: and it gave rise to a concept people call Chevron deference.
sentences.zh: 它引出了一个人们称之为“雪佛龙尊重”（Chevron deference）的概念。

sentences.en: And this is going to sound technical, but it's important.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能很专业，但很重要。

sentences.en: What that case says is if a law passed by Congress is ambiguous, then the agency gets to decide what the correct interpretation of that statute is.
sentences.zh: 该案的裁决是：如果国会通过的法律含糊不清，那么机构有权决定该法规的正确解释是什么。

sentences.en: And so long as it's a reasonable interpretation, the courts defer to the agency.
sentences.zh: 只要是合理的解释，法院就会尊重该机构的意见。

sentences.en: The short of it is that agencies which regulate all kinds of aspects of American life, the environment, the workplace, the marketplace, at the margin, but it's a wide margin,
sentences.zh: 简而言之，那些监管美国生活方方面面的机构——环境、工作场所、市场——在边缘地带，虽然是宽泛的边缘地带，

sentences.en: get to make the key decisions about how to implement a congressional statute.
sentences.zh: 有权就如何执行国会法规做出关键决定。

sentences.en: Essentially that if the law as written is confusing or has different interpretations, what this precedent says is that the federal agency, say the EPA, for example,
sentences.zh: 本质上，如果法律条文令人困惑或有不同解读，这个先例说的是联邦机构，比如 EPA，

sentences.en: should be able to decide how to interpret it.
sentences.zh: 应该有权决定如何解读它。

sentences.en: Like they don't need permission from Congress.
sentences.zh: 就像他们不需要国会的许可一样。

sentences.en: It doesn't fall to a judge.
sentences.zh: 这不归法官管。

sentences.en: It's the federal agency itself that governs the thing.
sentences.zh: 是联邦机构自己在管理这件事。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there's a logic to it.
sentences.zh: 所以这背后是有逻辑的。

sentences.en: These are complicated statutes and complicated regulatory areas.
sentences.zh: 这些都是复杂的法规和复杂的监管领域。

sentences.en: And you might want the experts to decide precisely how it applies.
sentences.zh: 你可能希望由专家来决定它具体如何应用。

sentences.en: That's one kind of argument.
sentences.zh: 这是一种论点。

sentences.en: What the opponents of the Chevron Doctrine say is that gives them too much power.
sentences.zh: 而“雪佛龙原则”的反对者认为，这赋予了他们太大的权力。

sentences.en: Congress, if it wants to do something, should say so.
sentences.zh: 国会如果想做什么，就应该明说。

sentences.en: And if Congress doesn't say so, the courts will step in and tell us what the law is.
sentences.zh: 如果国会没明说，法院就会介入并告诉我们法律是什么。

sentences.en: And Adam, tell me about the case this term that the justices have taken up.
sentences.zh: Adam，跟我讲讲本届任期内大法官们受理的那个案子。

sentences.en: It involves herring fishermen in Cape May, New Jersey, who a federal law says have to bring federal observers,
sentences.zh: 它涉及新泽西州开普梅的鲱鱼渔民，联邦法律规定他们必须携带联邦观察员，

sentences.en: federal monitors on their boats to make scientific assessments and to make sure that there's not overfishing.
sentences.zh: 即在船上配备联邦监督员，以进行科学评估并确保没有过度捕捞。

sentences.en: The fishermen say they have no problem with that.
sentences.zh: 渔民们说他们对此没有意见。

sentences.en: But the law doesn't say who pays for these monitors.
sentences.zh: 但法律没有说明谁来支付这些监督员的费用。

sentences.en: And the Federal Maritime Agency says the fishermen should pay for the monitors.
sentences.zh: 联邦海事局说应该由渔民支付监督员的费用。

sentences.en: And the fishermen object to that, both as a practical matter, they don't want to pay for it, but also as a kind of theoretical matter,
sentences.zh: 渔民们对此表示反对，既是出于实际考虑，他们不想付钱，也是出于某种理论上的考虑，

sentences.en: saying Congress hasn't said so explicitly and we shouldn't defer to the agency's interpretation of who has to pay.
sentences.zh: 他们认为国会没有明确说明，我们不应该尊重机构关于谁该付钱的解释。

sentences.en: That should get a fresh look from the courts.
sentences.zh: 这应该由法院重新审视。

sentences.en: And what is your sense of how the justices might rule on this?
sentences.zh: 你觉得大法官们会如何裁决？

sentences.en: The justices are hostile to Chevron, have not themselves invoked it in years, although lower courts continue to.
sentences.zh: 大法官们对“雪佛龙原则”持敌视态度，多年来他们自己都没有援引过它，尽管下级法院仍在继续使用。

sentences.en: And that gives you the feeling that this could be yet another precedent like abortion, like affirmative action, a major precedent overturned by the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这让你感觉这可能成为另一个像堕胎权、平权行动那样的重大先例，被最高法院推翻。

sentences.en: I think Chevron's days might be numbered, and that will be a very significant move if the court indeed does overrule it.
sentences.zh: 我认为“雪佛龙原则”的日子可能不多了，如果法院真的推翻它，那将是一个非常重大的举动。

sentences.en: It would essentially take power away from the government to regulate business.
sentences.zh: 这本质上会剥夺政府监管商业的权力。

sentences.en: It would take power away from the executive branch, away from agencies, and it would nominally, and here's the key point, it would nominally empower Congress.
sentences.zh: 它会从行政部门、从机构手中夺走权力，名义上——这是关键点——它会名义上赋予国会权力。

sentences.en: It would say, Congress, you decide what the law is, but because we have a wholly dysfunctional Congress,
sentences.zh: 它会说，国会，由你们来决定法律是什么，但因为我们有一个完全失能的国会，

sentences.en: what it in effect does is transfer power to the judiciary and to the Supreme Court in particular.
sentences.zh: 它实际上所做的是将权力转移给了司法部门，特别是最高法院。

sentences.en: And what does the Biden administration think about this?
sentences.zh: 拜登政府对此怎么看？

sentences.en: The Biden administration, in a brief in the case, said that overruling Chevron would be a convulsive shock to the legal system.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府在案件摘要中表示，推翻“雪佛龙原则”将对法律体系造成剧烈冲击。

sentences.en: It says that this is a workable arrangement, a sensible arrangement, that people and agencies and business groups have organized their lives around for decades,
sentences.zh: 它说这是一个可行的、合理的安排，几十年来人们、机构和商业团体都是围绕它来组织生活的，

sentences.en: and that there's no good reason to throw away this precedent.
sentences.zh: 没有充分的理由抛弃这个先例。

sentences.en: But Sabrina, I don't expect every attack on the regular story state to succeed.
sentences.zh: 但 Sabrina，我不认为对监管机构的每一次攻击都能成功。

sentences.en: We'll hear an argument this morning in case 22-448, Consumer Financial Protection Bureau versus the Community Financial Services Association.
sentences.zh: 今天上午我们将审理 22-448 号案件，即消费者金融保护局诉社区金融服务协会案。

sentences.en: Last week, the court heard arguments in a challenge to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which is a consumer watchdog that protects consumers in banking, credit card,
sentences.zh: 上周，法院听取了对消费者金融保护局（CFPB）的挑战，这是一个保护消费者在银行、信用卡、

sentences.en: and all kinds of other transactions.
sentences.zh: 以及各类其他交易中权益的消费者监督机构。

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court, this case is about checks and balances.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，法庭请允许我发言，本案关乎制衡。

sentences.en: One of Congress's most important checks on executive power is its power of the purse.
sentences.zh: 国会对行政权力最重要的制衡之一就是其“钱袋子”权力。

sentences.en: And the question in the case is whether the way the CFPB is funded through a request to the Federal Reserve System for the amount of money it thinks it needs up to a fairly high cap is constitutional.
sentences.zh: 本案的问题在于，CFPB 通过向美联储系统申请其认为所需的资金（最高限额相当高）来获得资助的方式是否符合宪法。

sentences.en: The challenge to the CFPB is that that funding mechanism gives it too much independence, too much power,
sentences.zh: 对 CFPB 的挑战在于，这种资助机制赋予了它太多的独立性和权力，

sentences.en: and the outcome of the ruling could be to say that that mechanism is unconstitutional, and therefore the agency is unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 裁决结果可能会宣布该机制违宪，从而导致该机构违宪。

sentences.en: But that attack on the CFPB got very little traction, even from the most conservative justices on the court.
sentences.zh: 但这种对 CFPB 的攻击几乎没有引起共鸣，即使是来自法院最保守的大法官们。

sentences.en: I get your point that this is different, that it's unique, that it's odd, that they've never gone this far.
sentences.zh: 我明白你的意思，这个案子很特别，很独特，很奇怪，他们以前从未走得这么远。

sentences.en: But not having gone this far is not a constitutional problem.
sentences.zh: 但没有走得这么远并不是一个宪法问题。

sentences.en: Justice Clarence Thomas said, yeah, it's true, it's odd, it's curious, it's novel, it's an interesting way to fund an agency, but that doesn't make it unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: Clarence Thomas 大法官说，是的，确实很奇怪，很新奇，这是一种资助机构的有趣方式，但这并不意味着它违宪。

sentences.en: And if you don't have Justice Clarence Thomas, and you're a conservative lawyer, you usually don't have a case.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有 Clarence Thomas 大法官的支持，而你又是一名保守派律师，你通常就没戏了。

sentences.en: So, this attack on an agency that business groups, many of them kind of hate because they're a very aggressive regulator, seems destined to fail.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种对商业团体（其中许多人因为他们是激进的监管者而讨厌他们）所支持的机构的攻击，似乎注定要失败。

sentences.en: And it's worth thinking about why that is.
sentences.zh: 值得思考一下为什么会这样。

sentences.en: I don't think it's because the court fundamentally disagrees with the general critique of the administrative state.
sentences.zh: 我不认为是因为法院从根本上不同意对行政国家的普遍批评。

sentences.en: But the cases that are reaching it are too ambitious, too aggressive, too bold.
sentences.zh: 而是因为送达法院的案件太雄心勃勃、太激进、太大胆了。

sentences.en: Okay, so when it comes to limiting the power of regulatory agencies, there are a few cases before the Supreme Court, and you're predicting a kind of mixed bag.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以当涉及到限制监管机构的权力时，最高法院面前有几个案子，你预测结果会是好坏参半。

sentences.en: Some wins, some losses.
sentences.zh: 有赢有输。

sentences.en: Let's turn to the next issue in front of the court, guns.
sentences.zh: 让我们转向法院面前的下一个议题：枪支。

sentences.en: So, last year, two terms ago, the court issued a major decision, and a major in two senses.
sentences.zh: 去年，也就是两个任期前，法院做出了一个重大裁决，这个“重大”有两层含义。

sentences.en: It struck down New York gun control law, and it said for the first time that you have a Second Amendment right to carry guns in public for self-defense.
sentences.zh: 它推翻了纽约的枪支管制法，并首次裁定你拥有宪法第二修正案赋予的在公共场合携带枪支进行自卫的权利。

sentences.en: So, that's huge.
sentences.zh: 所以，这非常重大。

sentences.en: But also huge was the standard the court announced that Justice Clarence Thomas announced about how you decide whether other gun control measures are constitutional or not.
sentences.zh: 但同样重大的是法院宣布的标准，即 Clarence Thomas 大法官宣布的关于如何判定其他枪支管制措施是否符合宪法的标准。

sentences.en: And remind me what that standard was, Adam.
sentences.zh: 提醒我一下那个标准是什么，Adam。

sentences.en: So, the standard, quite novel, draws on originalism, which is the idea that you want to figure out what the Constitution meant when it was adopted.
sentences.zh: 这个标准相当新颖，借鉴了原旨主义，即你想要弄清楚宪法在通过时意味着什么。

sentences.en: And what Justice Thomas said is that you have to go back in history and figure out whether there was analogous regulation, which is to say,
sentences.zh: Clarence Thomas 大法官说的是，你必须回顾历史，看看是否存在类似的法规，也就是说，

sentences.en: you have to find some regulation back in the day that was more or less similar.
sentences.zh: 你必须找到一些过去或多或少相似的法规。

sentences.en: It doesn't have to be, he says, a historical twin, but it has to map on to the modern law pretty well.
sentences.zh: 他说，它不必是历史上的“双胞胎”，但它必须与现代法律有很好的对应关系。

sentences.en: And unless you can find an analogous regulation, it's unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 除非你能找到类似的法规，否则它就是违宪的。

sentences.en: So, that's hardcore originalism, and it has really caused lower courts a lot of distress because they're not historians.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是硬核原旨主义，它确实给下级法院带来了很多困扰，因为他们不是历史学家。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we now have a case that's going to test whether the court is really serious about this methodology.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有一个案子，将考验法院是否真的认真对待这种方法论。

sentences.en: It involves a guy named Zaki Rahimi.
sentences.zh: 它涉及一个叫 Zaki Rahimi 的人。

sentences.en: And he was the subject of a domestic violence restraining order, and rightly so, because he was a, how to put this?
sentences.zh: 他是家庭暴力限制令的对象，理应如此，因为他是一个……该怎么说呢？

sentences.en: He did a lot of bad things with guns, including by threatening women, including by shooting them in public in road rage incidents,
sentences.zh: 他用枪做了很多坏事，包括威胁女性，包括在路怒事件中在公共场合向她们开枪，

sentences.en: or once when a friend of his didn't get the fast food order that he wanted.
sentences.zh: 或者有一次是因为他的朋友没买到他想要的快餐。

sentences.en: My God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: But how is this case testing originalism and historical analogies?
sentences.zh: 但这个案子是如何考验原旨主义和历史类比的？

sentences.en: So, he's convicted under this federal law that says if you're subject to such an order, you can't have a gun.
sentences.zh: 他根据这项联邦法律被定罪，该法律规定如果你受到此类限制令的约束，你就不能拥有枪支。

sentences.en: He's found with a gun.
sentences.zh: 他被发现持有枪支。

sentences.en: He's convicted.
sentences.zh: 他被定罪了。

sentences.en: And the Fifth Circuit says, well, wait a second.
sentences.zh: 第五巡回上诉法院说，等等。

sentences.en: In the founding era, there were no such things as domestic violence restraining orders.
sentences.zh: 在建国时代，根本没有家庭暴力限制令这种东西。

sentences.en: And therefore, the law is unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 因此，该法律违宪。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, that's the Fifth Circuit saying, hey, the new standard is history.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第五巡回法院在说，嘿，新标准是历史。

sentences.en: Here you go.
sentences.zh: 给你。

sentences.en: History.
sentences.zh: 历史。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, I mean, this is telling, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，这很能说明问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's kind of unsurprising that this form of judicial order didn't exist at a time when, in most places, women had very few rights.
sentences.zh: 因为在大多数地方女性几乎没有什么权利的时代，这种司法命令不存在，这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: So, you can tell there's a kind of disconnect between the standard announced by Justice Thomas and trying to implement it.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出，Clarence Thomas 大法官宣布的标准与试图实施它之间存在一种脱节。

sentences.en: And I have to think that the gun rights folks are quite unhappy that this is the follow-on case.
sentences.zh: 我不得不认为，拥枪权支持者们对这是后续案件感到非常不满。

sentences.en: Why, Adam?
sentences.zh: 为什么，Adam？

sentences.en: Because it's factually unattractive.
sentences.zh: 因为从事实层面来看，它很不讨喜。

sentences.en: It's sort of theoretically unattractive.
sentences.zh: 从理论层面来看，它也有些不讨喜。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, this is probably a case where there's some overreach from the Fifth Circuit,
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能是一个第五巡回法院有些越权的案子，

sentences.en: where the Supreme Court may well decide that this federal law that disarms people subject to domestic violence restraining orders, even under the history standard,
sentences.zh: 最高法院很可能会裁定，这项解除家庭暴力限制令对象武装的联邦法律，即使按照历史标准，

sentences.en: is constitutional.
sentences.zh: 也是符合宪法的。

sentences.en: But it's going to have to do some work to get there.
sentences.zh: 但它必须做一些工作才能达到那个结论。

sentences.en: So, those are a few of the big cases already on the court's docket.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些是法院案卷中已经存在的一些大案子。

sentences.en: But the court is very likely to hear another case and return to the area in which it has caused the most upheaval in recent years, abortion.
sentences.zh: 但法院很有可能还会审理另一个案子，并回到近年来引起最大动荡的领域：堕胎。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33 位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨 4 点 30 分给总统打电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 Super Sundays.
sentences.zh: 60 个超级星期天。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮助您了解世界，充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享特别优惠，请访问nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: Okay, so there's a case that you're expecting that will be taken up by the court, not on the docket yet, but probably will be.
sentences.zh: 好的，目前有一桩大家都在期待的案件，法院将会受理，虽然还没列入日程，但很可能会受理。

sentences.en: And that is abortion.
sentences.zh: 那就是堕胎案。

sentences.en: What is this case about?
sentences.zh: 这起案件是关于什么的？

sentences.en: Remind us, Adam.
sentences.zh: 提醒我们一下，亚当。

sentences.en: So this case follows, of course, the 2022 Dobbs decision, which did away with the constitutional right to abortion.
sentences.zh: 这起案件当然是紧随2022年的“多布斯案”判决而来，该判决废除了宪法赋予的堕胎权。

sentences.en: But it allowed states that wanted to have abortion to continue to do so.
sentences.zh: 但它允许那些希望保留堕胎权的州继续这样做。

sentences.en: And anti-abortion groups saw another line of attack.
sentences.zh: 而反堕胎组织看到了另一种攻击途径。

sentences.en: More than half of all pregnancy terminations these days involve an abortion pill called mifepristone.
sentences.zh: 如今，超过一半的妊娠终止手术涉及一种名为米非司酮的堕胎药。

sentences.en: And they make the argument that 20 years ago, the FDA was wrong to approve this pill, that it was unsafe.
sentences.zh: 他们提出的论点是，20年前FDA批准这种药是错误的，它是不安全的。

sentences.en: And they obtained a sweeping injunction from a trial judge.
sentences.zh: 他们从一位初审法官那里获得了一项广泛的禁令。

sentences.en: It goes to the Fifth Circuit, and the Fifth Circuit says, well, we're not going to go that far.
sentences.zh: 案件上诉到第五巡回法院，第五巡回法院表示，好吧，我们不会走那么远。

sentences.en: But we are going to cut back in significant ways, in ways that are particularly significant in light of Dobbs.
sentences.zh: 但我们要进行重大削减，考虑到“多布斯案”，这些削减尤为重要。

sentences.en: We're going to say that you can't get the pill by telemedicine, and you can't have it mailed to you, which makes it much, much harder for women,
sentences.zh: 我们要说的是，你不能通过远程医疗获取这种药，也不能邮寄给你，这让女性变得非常非常困难，

sentences.en: and particularly women in red states where abortion is banned or severely restricted, from having access to this pill.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对于那些堕胎被禁止或受到严格限制的红州的女性来说，获取这种药变得更加困难。

sentences.en: So it's a very significant case.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一起非常重大的案件。

sentences.en: It has already reached the Supreme Court once, and the Supreme Court has paused the injunction.
sentences.zh: 它已经上诉到最高法院一次，最高法院已经暂停了该禁令。

sentences.en: So today, the pill remains as available as ever.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，这种药依然像往常一样可以获得。

sentences.en: But it's less clear what will happen when, and I think the correct way to put this is when, when the court agrees to hear the case and probably by June renders a judgment.
sentences.zh: 但当法院同意审理此案，并可能在六月做出判决时，情况会如何还不清楚，我认为用“当”这个词是准确的。

sentences.en: And this is important not only for abortion, but to return to the question of administrative law.
sentences.zh: 这不仅对堕胎问题很重要，而且回到了行政法的问题上。

sentences.en: This would be the first time ever that a court would tell the FDA, an expert agency, that it had gotten the science wrong and that judges, not medical experts,
sentences.zh: 这将是法院有史以来第一次告诉FDA这个专家机构，它在科学上搞错了，而且法官而非医学专家，

sentences.en: would make the call on whether and how this abortion pill should be available.
sentences.zh: 将决定这种堕胎药是否以及如何提供。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this case was a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这起案件意义重大。

sentences.en: We covered it on the show because the implications, of course, would be huge.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中报道了它，因为其影响当然是巨大的。

sentences.en: It would reach across all states, blue and red, and, and restrict this pill that's been so widely used, you know, increasingly over the years and particularly since Dobbs.
sentences.zh: 它将波及所有州，无论是蓝州还是红州，并将限制这种多年来被广泛使用，尤其是“多布斯案”之后使用日益频繁的药物。

sentences.en: And it's another case, Sabrina, where you could make the argument that it has shaky foundations.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，这也是另一个你可以论证其基础不稳的案件。

sentences.en: The plaintiffs in the case may well not have legal standing, meaning they might not have suffered the sort of injury that gives them the right to sue.
sentences.zh: 案件的原告很可能没有法律地位，这意味着他们可能没有遭受那种赋予他们起诉权的伤害。

sentences.en: They are doctors, but they're doctors who don't perform abortions, including medication abortions.
sentences.zh: 他们是医生，但他们是不进行堕胎手术（包括药物流产）的医生。

sentences.en: So it's a little hard to see what their connection is to the case.
sentences.zh: 所以很难看出他们与这起案件有什么联系。

sentences.en: And this FDA approval is decades old.
sentences.zh: 而且FDA的这项批准已经是几十年前的事了。

sentences.en: It was approved in 2000, if I remember correctly.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，它是2000年批准的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the statute of limitations for bringing these suits is six years.
sentences.zh: 提起这些诉讼的诉讼时效是六年。

sentences.en: So you do the math and the lawsuit would seem to have been filed too late.
sentences.zh: 所以你算一下，这起诉讼似乎提起的太晚了。

sentences.en: So there are problems with the case.
sentences.zh: 所以这起案件存在问题。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's a larger, more conceptual problem for the Supreme Court, because when they issued the Dobbs decision, their rationale was we're getting out of the abortion business.
sentences.zh: 对于最高法院来说，还有一个更大、更概念性的问题，因为当他们做出“多布斯案”判决时，他们的理由是我们不再插手堕胎事务。

sentences.en: We're going to let the people's representatives decided this is not for judges.
sentences.zh: 我们要让人民的代表来决定，这不是法官的事。

sentences.en: We're done with abortion.
sentences.zh: 我们不再管堕胎了。

sentences.en: And it would be a hell of a move for them then just a couple of years later to say, but you know what?
sentences.zh: 如果他们仅仅几年后就说，但你知道吗？

sentences.en: We got a lot more to say about abortion.
sentences.zh: 关于堕胎我们还有很多话要说，那将是一个惊人的举动。

sentences.en: So once again, the conservatives are kind of rushing through an open door, but with a case that's not exactly a slam dunk.
sentences.zh: 所以保守派再次冲进了一扇敞开的门，但案件本身并不完全是十拿九稳的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what this term is going to tell us is whether the Supreme Court, which has sent signals that it is receptive to cases brought by conservatives,
sentences.zh: 所以本届任期将告诉我们，最高法院是否会像它所发出的信号那样，对保守派提起的案件持开放态度，

sentences.en: may not be receptive to all cases brought by conservatives, because there are places at least in which the right is moving too quickly, even for the tastes of this court.
sentences.zh: 但也可能不会对保守派提起的每一项案件都持开放态度，因为至少在某些方面，右翼的行动速度太快了，即使对这个法院的口味来说也是如此。

sentences.en: So, Adam, I want to talk about the broader context here, because, you know, when I think forward, of course, these cases are going to be decided in the middle of an election.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，我想谈谈这里更广泛的背景，因为你知道，当我展望未来时，这些案件当然会在选举期间做出裁决。

sentences.en: At the same time, the justices themselves have been under a lot of scrutiny about whether they're too cozy with political operatives.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，大法官们本身也受到了很多审查，关于他们是否与政治操盘手走得太近。

sentences.en: You know, I'm thinking Justice Thomas failing to disclose gifts from a wealthy Republican donor.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在想托马斯大法官未能披露来自一位富有共和党捐赠者的礼物。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if you think both of those pieces of context will have an effect on the way this term plays out.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否认为这两个背景因素会对本届任期的走向产生影响。

sentences.en: So it's hard to say definitively, because there are a lot of cross currents and a lot of unknowns, and the court's not particularly transparent.
sentences.zh: 很难下定论，因为有很多交叉的潮流和许多未知数，而且法院也不是特别透明。

sentences.en: But I think you're right, Sabrina, that these twin shadows of politics and ethics scandals will affect the court.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你是对的，萨布丽娜，政治和道德丑闻的双重阴影会影响法院。

sentences.en: The justices over the summer were many of them out in public talking about their eagerness to have an ethics code, and they say they're at work on that.
sentences.zh: 大法官们在夏天时，许多人在公开场合谈论他们渴望制定道德准则，并表示他们正在为此努力。

sentences.en: And that means they're at least sensitive to the public perception.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们至少对公众的看法很敏感。

sentences.en: Just as Thomas did the other day, recuse himself from a case involving his former law clerk and former Trump lawyer, John Eastman,
sentences.zh: 就像托马斯大法官前几天做的那样，他回避了一起涉及他前法律助理、前特朗普律师约翰·伊斯特曼的案件，

sentences.en: involving Eastman's efforts to subvert the election.
sentences.zh: 该案涉及伊斯特曼颠覆选举的努力。

sentences.en: And that's a step.
sentences.zh: 那是一个进步。

sentences.en: So we have a court that's under all kinds of pressure, and you might think that they don't want this to be the biggest term or the third term in a row,
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一个承受着各种压力的法院，你可能会认为他们不希望这成为最重大的任期，或者连续第三个任期，

sentences.en: where it's just blockbuster after blockbuster.
sentences.zh: 全是重磅炸弹式的案件。

sentences.en: So, Adam, we obviously don't know the answer yet, because, you know, these cases have yet to be argued.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，我们显然还不知道答案，因为你知道，这些案件还有待辩论。

sentences.en: But just to summarize here for a minute, there might be at least one big win for conservatives if the court overturns the Chevron precedent, the thing you described to me.
sentences.zh: 但简单总结一下，如果法院推翻了你向我描述的雪佛龙先例，保守派可能会取得至少一场大胜。

sentences.en: But otherwise, this term may end up disappointing conservatives, like they got greedy and this term told them no.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，本届任期最终可能会让保守派失望，就像他们太贪心了，而本届任期对他们说了不。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想那是对的。

sentences.en: But it's early days.
sentences.zh: 但现在还为时过早。

sentences.en: There are other cases on the horizon that we don't even know about.
sentences.zh: 还有其他我们甚至还不知道的案件即将出现。

sentences.en: There may be cases arising out of the election.
sentences.zh: 可能会有因选举而产生的案件。

sentences.en: There are efforts around the country to knock Donald Trump off the ballot.
sentences.zh: 全国各地都在努力将唐纳德·特朗普从选票中剔除。

sentences.en: Those could reach the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这些案件可能会上诉到最高法院。

sentences.en: So it's October.
sentences.zh: 所以现在是十月。

sentences.en: It's a long way till June.
sentences.zh: 距离六月还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: The term could take many different directions.
sentences.zh: 本届任期可能会有许多不同的走向。

sentences.en: But on the evidence of these early cases, this may be a term in which a conservative court pushes back against the right.
sentences.zh: 但根据这些早期案件的证据，这可能是一个保守派法院反击右翼的任期。

sentences.en: And I wonder, you know, if that will tell us something bigger about the movement, like this decades-long,
sentences.zh: 我想知道，这是否会告诉我们关于这场运动的更深层的东西，比如这几十年来，

sentences.en: very intentional effort to push the country to the right through the courts.
sentences.zh: 通过法院将国家推向右翼的非常刻意的努力。

sentences.en: So the court continues to have a six-justice conservative supermajority, all appointed by Republicans, and it will continue to move the law to the right.
sentences.zh: 所以法院继续拥有六名保守派大法官的绝对多数，全部由共和党人任命，它将继续推动法律向右转。

sentences.en: The question, though, is how fast?
sentences.zh: 问题是，速度有多快？

sentences.en: So it's a question, Sabrina, not of direction, but of velocity.
sentences.zh: 所以萨布丽娜，这不是方向的问题，而是速度的问题。

sentences.en: Adam, thank you.
sentences.zh: 亚当，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wenna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘文娜。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一《Connections》，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫联觉的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问nytimes.com/games立即开始游戏。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的事情。

sentences.en: The conflict in the Middle East deepened on Monday, with Israel's defense minister ordering what he called a complete siege of the long-blockaded Gaza Strip.
sentences.zh: 周一，中东冲突加剧，以色列国防部长下令对长期被封锁的加沙地带实施他所谓的“全面围困”。

sentences.en: Israel also hit the area with retaliatory airstrikes that destroyed buildings, including a mosque and a marketplace.
sentences.zh: 以色列还对该地区进行了报复性空袭，摧毁了包括一座清真寺和一个市场在内的建筑物。

sentences.en: Israel said the strikes were aimed at Hamas, the militant group that controls Gaza, and that launched the deadly attack on Israel over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 以色列表示，这些袭击的目标是控制加沙的激进组织哈马斯，该组织在周末对以色列发动了致命袭击。

sentences.en: Later in the day, Hamas threatened to execute one Israeli civilian hostage every time Israel hit Gazans in their homes without warnings with an airstrike.
sentences.zh: 当天晚些时候，哈马斯威胁说，每当以色列在没有警告的情况下对加沙平民的家园进行空袭时，他们就会处决一名以色列平民人质。

sentences.en: At least 150 Israelis were taken hostage by Palestinian assailants in the weekend's attack.
sentences.zh: 在周末的袭击中，至少有150名以色列人被巴勒斯坦武装人员扣为人质。

sentences.en: Israel's military said it had regained control over the Israeli border communities where the incursion had happened, but acknowledged that the fighting was still ongoing.
sentences.zh: 以色列军方表示，已重新控制了发生入侵的以色列边境社区，但承认战斗仍在继续。

sentences.en: 800 Israelis and 687 Palestinians have been killed in the violence so far.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，暴力冲突已造成800名以色列人和687名巴勒斯坦人死亡。

sentences.en: And the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Professor Claudia Golden for her work studying women in the labor market.
sentences.zh: 诺贝尔经济学奖授予了克劳迪娅·戈尔丁教授，以表彰她对劳动力市场中女性的研究。

sentences.en: Her research into subjects like the causes of the gender pay gap have had a profound impact on the field of labor economics.
sentences.zh: 她对性别薪酬差距成因等课题的研究对劳动经济学领域产生了深远影响。

sentences.en: She is the third woman to win the prize and the first to be honored solo.
sentences.zh: 她是第三位获得该奖项的女性，也是第一位单独获奖的女性。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Luke van der Ploeg, Jessica Chung, and Olivia Natt.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由Rob Zipko、Luke van der Ploeg、Jessica Chung和Olivia Natt制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Patricia Willens and Liz O'Balen.
sentences.zh: 由Patricia Willens和Liz O'Balen编辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Dan Powell and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 包含Dan Powell的原创音乐，由Alyssa Moxley进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansvork of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的Jim Brunberg和Ben Lansvork创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党就陷入了一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《Metro》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你收听播客的地方收听。
